_comment: The single source of truth for 'is this utterance only a greeting?', shared by every surface
that has to answer one: intents.py (typed chat AND, by import, the box microphone via
It exists because those surfaces each carried their own copy and all three had drifted apart,
in ways nobody could see until a human hit one. The Python copy classified 'how are you' as a
greeting -- 'how' is a prefix of 'howdy' -- and answered a question with 'Yes, sir.'. The
voice-bridge copy used str.startswith on a tuple, so 'Jarvis, hit the lights' was a greeting
because 'hit' begins with 'hi', and the command was silently dropped.
'phrases' is matched by EXACT equality after normalisation (lowercase, punctuation to spaces,
whitespace collapsed). No prefix matching, no word decomposition, no length heuristics --
every one of those is how the bugs above got in.
Adding a phrase here saves one LLM turn (~20 s on this box). Adding one wrongly answers a real
question with a pleasantry. Those costs are not symmetric: when in doubt, leave it out and let
the model answer. 'how are you', 'what's up' and 'are you ok' are questions and are absent on
purpose -- the model answers them well ('I am functioning as expected.', measured).
'not_greetings' is the regression set: every entry MUST reach the model. Both test suites
assert both lists, so a change here fails in Python and JavaScript together.
not_greetings: there is a problem with the fan
hey jarvis, turn off the fan
good morning, remind me to call mum at 9
